title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. The base is R = Spf Λ, where Λ is a complete local ring with residue field k of characteristic p. Over k we are given p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) groups M_0 and N_0. As the NB about E_0 and the connected–étale sequence indicate, M_0 is étale. N_0 is at first of multiplicative type ('de t.m.') and later only connected ('radiciel', reading uncertain). Grothendieck studies the formal moduli of extensions E of lifts M of M_0 by lifts N of N_0, with a prescribed special fibre. Earlier pages show this deformation problem is pro-representable and compatible with base change, so it is a 'modular' situation.

(1) Moduli of lifts of the trivial extension ξ_0. Call it 𝓜_{ξ0}. Étale and multiplicative-type groups lift uniquely, so 𝓜_{ξ0}(S) = Ker(Ext^1_S(M,N) → Ext^1_k(M_0,N_0)). This kernel is a group functor, so 𝓜_{ξ0} is a smooth formal group over Spf Λ. Concretely, for M étale and N multiplicative it is Hom_{Z_p}(T_p M, N^) = T_p(M_0)^∨ ⊗ N^. This is a formal torus. Formal tori are rigid, so it is determined by its special fibre: the (possibly twisted) formal torus T_p(M_0)^∨ ⊗ N_0. This is exactly the structure behind Serre–Tate local moduli of ordinary abelian varieties and ordinary BT groups, read off from Ext(étale, multiplicative).

(2) For a general extension class ξ over k, the moduli 𝓜_ξ of lifts is a torsor under 𝓜_{ξ0}. This is because Ext over S surjects onto Ext over k, and the fibres are cosets of the kernel. A bracketed remark, only partly legible, says this torsor is not in general of a special or trivial kind and links this to a theorem of Tate on lifts of p-divisible groups.

(3) Generalisation: N_0 is now only connected/radicial, not multiplicative, while M_0 is still étale. E_0 determines M_0, N_0 and the extension via the connected–étale sequence. Since M lifts uniquely, sending an extension to its sub gives a natural morphism X = 𝓜_{E_0} → 𝓜_{N_0} = Y to the formal moduli of N_0. This morphism makes X a torsor under 𝒩_Y ⊗_{Z_p} T_p(E_0)^∨_Y, i.e. Hom(T_p M, 𝒩) over Y, where 𝒩 is the universal deformation of N_0. Note T_p(E_0) = T_p(M_0), because N_0 is connected. Hence the structure of 𝓜_{E_0} reduces to that of 𝓜_{N_0}. When N_0 is multiplicative, Y is a point and one recovers (1)–(2).

The next page goes on to functoriality: pairs of extensions compatible with given maps u, v. These are represented infinitesimally as a kernel of α − β between groups of the form T_p(·)^∨ ⊗ (·).
errors: The hypothesis that M_0 is étale is used but not restated on this page. It is needed for unique lifting of M and for T_p(E_0) = T_p(M_0).

'T_p(M_0)^∨ ⊗ N_0' should be read as the formal (connected) part, i.e. Hom(T_p M_0, N_0^). As a p-divisible group, T_p^∨ ⊗ N_0 is the BT group whose formal group is the torus; the notation is loose but harmless.

Over a complete local base, a torsor under a formally smooth formal group with a k-point admits a section, so it is non-canonically trivial. Whatever the bracket asserts (an obstruction tied to Tate's theorem) can only concern non-canonical triviality or the absence of a canonical (Serre–Tate-type) origin, not genuine non-triviality. The bracket is too illegible to judge.

ideas.what: Formal moduli of extensions of an étale BT group by a multiplicative one is the formal torus T_p(M)^∨ ⊗ N^, determined by its special fibre
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate coordinates / Serre–Tate local moduli of ordinary p-divisible groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate (1964 Woods Hole); written up by Messing (1972) and Katz ('Serre–Tate local moduli', 1981)
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Grothendieck's ICM Nice 1970 talk and the Montréal notes 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974); unsure

ideas.what: Moduli of lifts of a nontrivial extension class is a torsor under the moduli of lifts of the trivial one
ideas.modern_name: torsor structure on deformation space of extensions

ideas.what: For E_0 with étale quotient and connected (non-multiplicative) sub, the deformation space of E_0 fibres over that of the connected part as a torsor under Hom(T_p M, 𝒩)
ideas.modern_name: fibration of deformation spaces along the connected–étale (slope) filtration; generalised Serre–Tate theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Messing; later Chai and Moonen (Serre–Tate theory for moduli of PEL type, ~2004), Chai's work on Hecke orbits and leaves

missed.claim: A pre-1970 manuscript record, tied to the 1966 Tate letter on crystals, of Grothendieck formulating the local moduli of BT groups with étale quotient as a torsor over the deformation space of the connected part. It includes the Serre–Tate formal-torus statement as the special case. This is historically interesting but mathematically standard today.
missed.quote: Ce dernier fait de 𝓜_{E_0} un torseur sous 𝒩_Y ⊗_{Z_p} T_p(E_0)^∨_Y. Donc la structure de 𝓜_{E_0} est connue si celle de 𝓜_{N_0}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's independent route to Serre–Tate-type structure via a modular Ext functor, before Messing and Katz. It does not add new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the Serre–Tate formal-torus description and its routine extension to a connected sub. Both are well established in Messing, Katz, Chai and Moonen. The interest is purely historical: the dating and Grothendieck's modular viewpoint.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'k' is struck out and replaced by 'R' followed by 'Spf Λ' ('sur [R], Spf Λ').
The insertion above 'tore' reads 'formel tordu' (approximately 'tore formel tordu').
In the bracket under 2), the reading 'pseudo-torseur' and 'lifts infini[té?]' are uncertain. The struck word 'formels' before 'p-divisibles' is correctly marked as deleted.
In 2), the subscript of 𝓜 is ξ (i.e. 𝓜_ξ); compare 𝓜_{ξ0} at the end of the line.
